newsitem.title: USA: Farrakhan wants U.S. shut down to honor march.
newsitem.headline: Farrakhan wants U.S. shut down to honor march.

text.p: Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan urged blacks on Monday to celebrate the second anniversary of the Million Man March by staying away from work Oct. 16 in a day of absence and atonement.

"We would like to shut the country down for one day, to say to America, look at what America would look like if we weren't here," Farrakhan said at a town hall meeting during the Southern Christian Leadership Convention's annual convention.

"Think about it. No porters to carry your bag and tote your barge. Nobody at the airport. Nobody to sing for you that day. Nobody to dance for you that day. Nobody to throw a basketball or a baseball or a football. All of us thinking about reconciling with God, reconciling with each other," Farrakhan said.

Farrakhan said the Oct. 16, 1995, march by black men on the Mall in Washington, D.C., should be remembered as a holy day of atonement, reconcilitation and responsibility. "In every city in America, we intend to have a day of atonement and a day of absence," he said.
He said the Nation of Islam also plans another Million Man March in the year 2000, with women and girlfriends also invited. "We want to start the new century properly," he said.

"On that day we want to remarry everybody that is married. And we hope to get 10,000 young people that wish to be married and marry them because the new century must be the century of family. Without strong family, you don't have strong community or strong nation," Farrakhan said.
